subject: Phase-pay prepay bridge: proposed ramp, exit math and refund mechanics
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elenap@catalystbio.com>, Ken Sato <ken.sato@catalystbio.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Phase-pay prepay bridge: proposed ramp, exit math and refund mechanics

Hi Elena / Ken —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a compact proposal that stitches together: a 3-year prepay with an annual phased payout structure (we call it PhasePay), a ramp schedule that maps to expected seat/usage cohorts, and an exit/refund waterfall that is designed to limit downside while preserving your budget predictability.

Key highlights in the attached PDF:
- Year 1: 40% prepay at signing, Year 2: 30% prepay at renewal, Year 3: 30% prepay (cohort option to shift up to 10% between years)
- Volume discounts tiered by committed monthly token throughput with clear breakpoints
- Early exit: 60-day notice + pro rata refund with a 10% administrative retention and step-down amortization on multi-year discounts (details in Section 4)

Two asks from your side to finalize:
1) Confirm whether you need co-terming across Catalyst business units or will sign per BU.
2) Any procurement/legal must-haves beyond SOC2 and audit logs we already covered.

I’ve cc’ed Lauren (pricing/SME) and Marcus (finance) for quick answers on the math. If this looks directionally right I can prepare a DocuSign packet with the redline-ready term sheet.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0178 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_MultiYear_PhasePay_Proposal_20270422.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
From: Elena Park <elenap@catalystbio.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@catalystbio.com, Ken Sato <ken.sato@catalystbio.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T14:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Phase-pay prepay bridge: proposed ramp, exit math and refund mechanics

Dylan —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. A few immediate points from procurement/legal that will drive internal approval:

1) Early termination refund cap: we cannot accept a full pro rata refund for multi-year prepay. Our finance team wants a predictable maximum refund liability on Redwood’s side; propose a 90-day refund cap or an escrow-style holdback that phases out over 12 months.

2) Co-terming: Catalyst prefers co-terming across business units where we can, but only if the provider accepts a single contract accounting treatment (i.e., one amortization schedule across the co-term).

3) Audit & data handling: you indicated SOC2; please include monthly usage reports and token-level cost breakdowns in the contract or appendix. That will be mandatory for our controller.

I’m attaching our procurement redlines. Please flag anything you consider a showstopper.

Elena Park
VP Procurement | Catalyst Bio
Attachment: Catalyst_redlines_v1.docx
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elenap@catalystbio.com>, procurement@catalystbio.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-23T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Phase-pay prepay bridge: proposed ramp, exit math and refund mechanics

Elena —

Appreciate the fast feedback and the redlines. I reviewed with Finance and Legal; below are high-level responses to your three asks. I’m marking items that require internal approval vs. negotiable commercial concessions.

1) Early termination refund cap: negotiable. Marcus proposes two alternative constructs (both intended to give you budget predictability while limiting Redwood’s tail risk):
   A) 90-day refund cap from effective termination date, net of actual usage and true-up (this meets your ask).
   B) Escrow-style holdback equal to 15% of total prepay, released pro rata over 12 months unless termination occurs — refunds then draw from the remaining balance under a pro rata formula.

2) Co-terming: acceptable only if Catalyst agrees to a single accounting amortization schedule and commits to a parent-level signature (so Redwood’s billing/recognition aligns). We can include language that allows BU-level seat transfers but keeps the parent as guarantor.

3) Monthly usage reports: no problem. We will supply token-level breakdowns and cost-per-route summaries via the Console export and a monthly CSV.

I’ve asked Rishi (legal) to prepare redline snippets for A and B so you can see language. If you prefer A we can move quickly — I can issue an updated term sheet and DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Next step: which refund construct do you prefer (A or B)?

Thanks,
Dylan
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-23T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Phase-pay prepay bridge: legal language + amortization snippet

Team —

I drafted two short contract snippets to cover both refund constructs. I’m pasting the plain-English summary here so we have consistent talking points for procurement:

- Option A (90-day cap): On early termination for convenience by Customer, Redwood will refund unused prepay amounts pro rata for a maximum refund period equal to ninety (90) days from the effective termination date. Any discounts applied at signing will be recaptured on amounts credited under the refund calculus at the same discount rate. Refunds will be net of actual usage through termination and a one-time administrative fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the refundable amount.

- Option B (Escrow holdback): Customer prepays in full. Redwood retains an escrowed holdback equal to fifteen percent (15%) of total prepay, released quarterly over twelve (12) months. If Customer terminates during the release window, Redwood will calculate refunds from the remaining escrow balance on a pro rata basis, after recapturing the portion of multi-year discount allocable to the refunded amount. Any disputes on usage will go to joint audit per Appendix C.

Marcus — per finance, what is the revenue recognition/commission impact if we accept B for a deal of this size (approx $4.5M list over three years)?

Rishi
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-24T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Phase-pay prepay bridge: legal language + amortization snippet

Quick finance note for the thread:

- For a $4.5M contracted value with the PhasePay split (40/30/30) and an overall 18% multi-year discount, Option A (90-day cap) produces a relatively straightforward liability profile: short-term refund reserve equal to 90 days of recognized revenue + 10% admin hold. This has minimal multi-period revenue revision risk and keeps ASC 606 amortization clean.

- Option B (Escrow holdback) increases the complexity for revenue recognition and commission deferral because the 15% holdback is effectively a performance-obligation-anchored liability that releases over 12 months. We can model it, but it requires quarterly adjustments and smaller near-term revenue recognition, which may impact commission draws for the AE.

If we need to be more competitive on headline refund exposure, recommend we accept Option A and tighten the discount recapture language (explicit recapture on refunded portion). That is the cleanest for accounting and sales compensation.

Marcus

Attachment: PhasePay_revenue_model_Q1.xlsx (referenced internally)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elenap@catalystbio.com>, procurement@catalystbio.com, Ken Sato <ken.sato@catalystbio.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-25T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Phase-pay prepay bridge: proposed ramp, exit math and refund mechanics

Elena / Ken —

Thanks for the transparency — based on internal alignment we can proceed with Option A (90-day refund cap) with two clarifications that should address both sides:

1) Refund calculation: Refunds will be pro rata for up to 90 days from termination, net of actual usage through termination and a 10% administrative fee. Multi-year discounts will be recaptured only on the refunded portion at the effective discount rate specified in the schedule.

2) Co-terming language: We will allow co-terming across BUs if Catalyst executes at the parent level; the parent signs as guarantor and the amortization schedule will be applied at the parent-contract level. BU transfers are supported subject to 30-day notice and headcount reconciliation.

I’ve updated the term sheet and attached the revised PDF and included a DocuSign link for signature if these two points are acceptable. If you want the escrow variant instead let me know and we’ll ask Finance to run the full ASC 606 impact model.

Next steps: sign the attached DocuSign packet and we’ll schedule kickoff for contract ops to set up billing/console access.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
